title: Auxiliary ample model of a positive power of a generic symmetric line
statement: Let $T$ be a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $h:H\to T$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$ and addition and inverse satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose each geometric fibre over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$ fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to H_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $T$, and assume $H_\eta$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Given an ample invertible module $M$ on $H_\eta$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] with $[-1]^*M\simeq M$ (tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]), there exist an affine open covering $T=\bigcup_i T_i$, integers $d_i\geq1$, invertible modules $N_i$ on $H_{T_i}$ and isomorphisms $N_i|_{H_\eta}\simeq M^{\otimes d_i}$, such that $N_i$ is relatively ample over $T_i$: its restriction over every affine open of $T_i$ is ample. Here $H_{T_i}$ is the restriction of $H$ to $T_i$. This is an existence assertion about an auxiliary ordinary line module, with no supplied line on $H$ and no cubical structure in its conclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-raynaud-generic-ample-symmetrization] with $S=T$, $G=H$, $p=h$ and $L=M$. Its hypotheses hold verbatim: $T$ is normal integral locally Noetherian since it is Noetherian; $h$ is smooth separated commutative of finite presentation with the specified semiabelian geometric fibres; and $M$ is ample and invertible on the generic fibre. The cited result needs neither properness of $H_\eta$ nor symmetry of $M$, so those extra hypotheses cause no restriction on its application. It supplies an affine open covering $T=\bigcup_iT_i$, positive integers $a_i$, relatively ample invertible modules $Q_i$ on $H_{T_i}$, and isomorphisms $(Q_i)_\eta\simeq(M\otimes[-1]^*M)^{\otimes a_i}$. In particular its relative ampleness assertion is over every affine open of each $T_i$, exactly the convention in this item.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.13, existing generic symmetrization prerequisite; original WANTED. Agent specialization using the supplied symmetry.

proof.text: Choose an isomorphism $\theta:[-1]^*M\simeq M$ supplied by the symmetry hypothesis. The map $\mathrm{id}_M\otimes\theta$ identifies $M\otimes[-1]^*M$ with $M\otimes M$. Taking its $a_i$-fold tensor product and regrouping the $2a_i$ factors gives $(M\otimes[-1]^*M)^{\otimes a_i}\simeq M^{\otimes 2a_i}$; in local frames this sends the tensor of $a_i$ pairs to the same ordered tensor of $2a_i$ factors, so it glues and is invertible. Put $N_i=Q_i$ and $d_i=2a_i\geq1$, and compose with the generic isomorphism of step 1. These are the required generic identifications. The same $N_i$ retain the relative ampleness supplied in step 1. This constructs only ordinary line modules, as required.
